claims.explanation: BIBX-1382 is an EGFR/ERBB2 tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and the most selectively killed lines are enriched for EGFR-pathway activation, either through EGFR mutation/amplification (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) or through downstream MAPK/PI3K activation such as KRAS, BRAF, PIK3CA, and ERBB3 alterations. Lines that are least affected tend to lack EGFR dependence and instead carry RAS/RAF mutations or PTEN loss that bypass EGFR blockade. Thus selectivity is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling, with EGFR mutation/expression and ERBB2 expression as sensitizing features and activating RAS/RAF mutations as protective.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are among the most killed; EGFR is the annotated target
Drug inhibits EGFR kinase; high EGFR expression/activation predicts dependence
ERBB2 is an annotated target of BIBX-1382; ERBB2-driven signaling would be blocked
KRAS-mutant lines (SNU410, CL11, OV7, KPNSI9S) are among least affected, bypassing EGFR blockade
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (LOXIMVI, UACC62, IGR37, IPC298) are least affected
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT downstream of EGFR, reducing dependence on EGFR
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, OV7) are among least affected, providing EGFR-independent PI3K signaling
NRAS-mutant lines (KU1919, IPC298) are least affected, bypassing EGFR
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK independent of EGFR; enriched in least-affected lines
ERBB3 mutation in SNUC5, a highly killed line, may enhance ERBB2/ERBB3 signaling dependence
TP53 mutation is common in both extremes and not selective; weak evidence
